title: Minimalization of bounded finite free resolution
statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], M an R-module, d a natural number, and P an exact augmented projective resolution of M [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence; def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Suppose P is zero above degree d and every term is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then there exists an exact augmented projective resolution Q of M, zero above degree d, with finite free terms, such that the image of each differential from degree i+1 to i, for i<d, is contained in the maximal ideal times Q_i.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00MT, applied in the proof of Tag 00OA to remove trivial summands

proof.text: Starting from this bounded finite free resolution, if some differential $\varphi_i:F_i\to F_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le d$ has a matrix coefficient that is a unit, apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-unit-entry-splits]. After changing bases, the underlying complex is the direct sum of a smaller finite free complex and the identity complex $R\xrightarrow{1}R$ in degrees $i$ and $i-1$. The augmentation $F_0\to M$ vanishes on that identity summand: when $i=1$, its $R$ in degree $0$ is the image of $\varphi_1$ and $\varepsilon\varphi_1=0$; when $i>1$, the identity summand has no degree-$0$ term. Thus the augmentation factors through the smaller complex. Since the identity summand is exact, the smaller augmented complex stays exact.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex), statement and proof, lines 24608--24650; its application in the proof of Lemma Tag 00OA, lines 26989--26994

proof.text: Repeat the preceding cancellation while a unit coefficient occurs in any differential. Each cancellation decreases the sum of the finite ranks of the two affected terms, so the process terminates. In the terminal complex every matrix coefficient of every differential is a nonunit; in a local ring every nonunit belongs to $\mathfrak m$, hence $\varphi_i(F_i)\subseteq\mathfrak mF_{i-1}$ for all $1\le i\le d$. The resulting exact sequence is the required minimal finite free resolution.

lean.statement:
theorem minimalize_bounded_finite_free_resolution {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R)
    (d : ℕ) (P : ProjectiveResolution M)
    (hzero : ∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (P.complex.X i))
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (P.complex.X i) ∧ Module.Free R (P.complex.X i)) :
    ∃ Q : ProjectiveResolution M,
      (∀ i : ℕ, d < i → IsZero (Q.complex.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, Module.Finite R (Q.complex.X i) ∧ Module.Free R (Q.complex.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, i < d →
        LinearMap.range (Q.complex.d (i + 1) i).hom ≤
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R • (⊤ : Submodule R (Q.complex.X i)))
